{White has made a serious mistake against the From's Gambit and Black already
has a winning attack. What should Black play?} 5... g4 {[%wrong There's a
better attacking move. Try again and look for a strong threat.] [%hint Chase
White's knight away from defending the kingside.]} 6. Nd4 {We are only on move
six and Black can already force checkmate! How should you do it?} Qh4+ {
[%wrong There's a stronger move. Try again and look for a way to force
checkmate.] [%hint Find a safe check on the e1-h4 diagonal.]} 7. g3 {Great
move! What's the most spectacular way to checkmate in two moves?} Qxg3+ {
[%wrong There's a better option. Try again and look for a quick checkmate.] 
[%hint Sacrifice your queen to open the e1-h4 diagonal.]} (7... Bxg3+ $5 {
This is a great move, but you get more style points for another forced mate.
Try to find it.}) 8. hxg3 {Wow! How can you finish the game?} Bxg3# {[%wrong
There's a better option. Try again and look for a checkmate.] [%hint Look for
a check. Is it mate?] This is the dream finish of any From's Gambit player.
Make sure to avoid it when you have the white pieces.} *

{The From's Gambit is tricky, but the well-prepared 1.f4 player doesn't need
to fear it. Black wants to play g4, Qh4+, and checkmate in the opening. How
should White defend?} 5. g3 {[%wrong There's a better move. Try again and look
for a way to block the kingside dark squares.] [%hint Place a pawn on the
e1-h4 diagonal to prevent any checkmate tricks.]} (5. d4 $5 {This idea of
meeting g4 with Ne5 is reasonable, but there's a kingside pawn advance that's
stronger. Try to find it.}) (5. e4 $2 g4 {White must sacrifice material to
prevent Qh4+ next turn. Try again and look for a safer move.}) (5. Nc3 $2 g4 {
White must sacrifice a knight to prevent a quick checkmate. Try again and look
for a safer move.}) (5. h3 $2 Bg3# {That's checkmate! Try to find a safer
kingside pawn move.}) (5. h4 $2 Bg3# {That's checkmate. Try to find a stronger
kingside pawn move.}) 5... g4 {Nice move! How should you save your knight?} 6.
Nh4 {[%wrong There's a better option. Try to find a safe knight move.] [%hint
Find a protected square for your knight, but don't retreat all the way to the
back rank.] Good work! White has a safe position and good chances to convert
the extra pawn into a win.} (6. Nd4 $5 {This is OK, but it's better to use
this knight to guard the kingside. How should you do it?}) (6. Ng1 $2 h5 {
Black has a powerful attack. Try again and look for a safer knight move to
block the kingside.}) *

undefended pawn.] Well played! White wins a pawn and should eventually win the
game.} *

{White has sacrificed a pawn in the dubious Grob Opening. How should Black
recapture on d5?} 5... exd5 {[%wrong There's a better option. Try again and
look for a good capture.] [%hint Recapture on d5, but keep the a4-e8 diagonal
blocked.]} (5... Qxd5 $2 6. Bxd5 {White wins the queen. Try again and look for
a stronger capture.}) (5... cxd5 $2 6. Qa4+ {White forks Black's king and
bishop. Try again and look for a stronger capture.}) 6. Qxb7 {Good idea! How
should you save your rook?} Nd7 {[%wrong White wins material. Try again and
look for a way to save your a8-rook.] [%hint Develop your knight so that your
queen protects the rook on a8.] Well played! Black has a much better center
and a lead in development. You can refute the terrible pawn grab, Qxc6?? in
the next challenge.} *

{White is temporarily up a pawn, but Black has a winning move . Try to find it.
} 7... Rc8 {[%wrong There's a much stronger option. Try again and look for a
decisive threat.] [%hint Skewer White's queen and bishop on the c-file.]} 8.
Qxd5 {White saved the queen, but not the game. What should black play?} Rxc1# {
[%wrong There's a stronger move. Try again and look for a way to end the game.]
[%hint Look for a check. Is it mate?] Well done! The Grob should favor Black
with precise play and is rarely seen at the top level.} *

{White thought that the e5 pawn could safely be captured, but Black can prove
otherwise. What should you play?} 7... Qh4+ {[%wrong There's a better move.
Try again and look for a strong forcing option.] [%hint Find a powerful check.]
} (7... Bxe5 $2 8. Bxc6+ {If bxc6 then Qh5+ keeps a material edge for White.
Try again and look for a stronger forcing option.}) 8. g3 {Great move! If
White doesn't target Black's queen then Bxe5 wins for Black. Now Black must be
precise. What's next?} Qe4 {[%wrong White is doing well. Try again and look
for the strongest queen move.] [%hint Save your queen and attack a rook.]} (
8... Qe7 $2 9. Bxd6 {White keeps an extra pawn and a good position. Try again
and look for a stronger queen move.}) 9. Bxd6 {Great idea! How should you win
material?} Qxh1 {[%wrong There's a better move. Try again and look for the
strongest capture.] [%hint Capture a rook.] Well played! Black has an extra
exchange and White has two minor pieces in danger!} (9... cxd6 $2 10. Qh5+ {
After g6 and Qf3 White is doing well. Try again and look for a stronger
capture.}) *

{How did GM Nakamura fight for the initiative before defending his e5-pawn?} 
5... Qh4+ {[%wrong There's a better move. Try again and look for a strong
check.] [%hint Find a good check.]} (5... f6 $5 {This is reasonable, but GM
Nakamura preferred a strong check. What was his idea?}) (5... exf4 $2 6. Bxg7 {
White wins the rook on h8. Try again and look for a better forcing option.}) (
5... Qe7 $2 6. Nf3 {The pin on the long diagonal gives White strong pressure
against e5. Try again and look for a way to insert a useful check before
bringing the queen to e7.}) 6. g3 {The pawn advance weakens the protection of
White's king. How should you save your queen and protect e5?} Qe7 {[%wrong
There's a better move. Try again and look for the safest square for your queen.
] [%hint Retreat your queen to support your e-pawn.]} (6... Qf6 $2 7. Nf3 {
The e5-pawn is pinned against Black's queen. Try again and look for a safer
queen move.}) 7. Nf3 {Nice move! How should you continue to support your
strong pawn center?} f6 {[%wrong White is doing well. Try again and look for
the best way to defend your e-pawn.] [%hint Defend e5 with another pawn.] Well
done! Black went to on to win a complicated game in Jobava - Nakamura, 2012.} (
7... Bg4 $5 {This is playable, but it's safer to defend e5 with another pawn.
How should you do it?}) (7... exf4 $2 8. Bxg7 {White wins material. Try again
and look for a way to defend the e5-pawn instead of moving it.}) (7... e4 $6 8.
Bxg7 {White wins material. Try again and look for a way to defend the e5-pawn
instead of moving it.}) *

{Black should not have captured on f4. How can White win material?} 6. Bxg7 {
[%wrong There's a stronger option. Try again and look for a useful capture.] 
[%hint Capture a pawn and trap a rook.]} (6. Bxc6+ $5 {This is reasonable, but
another capture is even stronger. Try to find it.}) (6. exf4 $2 Qh4+ {Black
has dangerous counterplay. Try again and look for a better capture.}) 6... Qh4+
{Nice move! How should you escape the check?} 7. Kf1 {[%wrong Illegal] [%hint
Hide your king on a safe square on the first rank.]} (7. g3 $2 fxg3 {Black
prepares a deadly discovered check. Try again and look for a strong king move.}
) (7. Ke2 $2 Qg4+ {Black wins the g7-bishop. Try again and look for a stronger
king move.}) 7... Nh6 {What should you capture?} 8. Bxh8 {[%wrong There's a
better move. Try again and look for the strongest capture.] [%hint Capture a
free rook.] Good work! White has a winning material advantage.} (8. Nf3 $5 {
This is a good idea, but let's try a strong capture.}) (8. Bxc6+ $2 bxc6 {
The bishop pair will give Black counterplay. Try again and look for a better
capture.}) (8. Bxh6 $2 Qxh6 {There's a much stronger capture. Try to find it.})

{Black's awkward bishop on d6 encourages a surprising developing move by White.
What piece should White bring out next?} 5. Na3 {[%wrong There's a better
developing move. Try again and look for the ideal square for a knight.] [%hint
Bring a knight to c4 as quickly as possible.]} (5. Be2 $5 {This is OK, but
most players prefer to develop the b1-knight. Where should it go?}) (5. Nf3 $2
e4 {Black gains space and forces the knight to move again. Try to find a
stronger move with the other knight.}) (5. d4 $2 exd4 {Black is happy to
exchange pawns and increase the scope of the d6-bishop. Try again and look for
a good developing move.}) (5. Bxc6 $2 dxc6 {Black has the bishop pair and a
comfortable position. Try again and look for a good knight move.}) (5. Nc3 $2
O-O {Surprsingly, there's a better square for this knight. Where should it go?}
) (5. Ne2 $2 a6 {White must exchange the b5-bishop so that it isn't trapped.
Try again and look for a stronger knight move.}) 5... O-O {Good start! Black
should have considered the equally odd-looking Na5 to prevent White's plan.
What should White play next?} 6. Nc4 {[%wrong There's a stronger move. Try
again and look for a good square for your a3-knight.] [%hint Target d6 and e5
with a knight.] Good work! White will soon win a pawn or at least damage
Black's structure and win the bishop pair with Nxd6.} (6. Bxc6 $2 dxc6 {
Black has the bishop pair and a comfortable position. Try again and look for a
good knight move.}) (6. Nf3 $2 e4 {Black chases the knight and wins a tempo.
Try again and look for a stronger knight move.}) (6. Ne2 $2 Ne7 {Black brings
the knight to g6 with a solid position. Try again and look for a stronger
knight move.}) 0-1

{White tried the Na3-c4 plan from the previous challenge against GM Dmitry
Andreikin, but here it didn't work out. How did Black prepare to win material?
} 9... Nb8 {[%wrong There's a much stronger move. Try to find it and check the
hint if you're stuck.] [%hint Retreat your knight and prepare to trap the
b5-bishop.]} (9... a6 $2 10. Bxc6 {White has a comfortable position. Try again
and look for a way to save your c6-knight.}) 10. Nf5 {What a move! White can't
untangle the bishop and knight on the queenside. How should Black win material?
} a6 {[%wrong There's a better move. Try again and look for a strong threat.] 
[%hint Trap the b5-bishop.]} (10... c6 $5 {This is a good move, but Black
preferred to attack the bishop another way. How did he do it?}) (10... g6 $5 {
This is OK, but Black preferred to target the b6-bishop. How did he do it?})
11. Ba4 {Nice move! How did GM Andreikin win material?} b5 {[%wrong There's
better option. Try again and look for a winning fork.] [%hint Fork bishop and
knight.] Black wins material and soon won the game. Well done!} (11... d5 $5 {
This is a good move, but Black preferred to win material with a fork. How did
he do it?}) 0-1
